::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"}
## Purpose

This document fixes the story of the manuscript: three research questions, the variables that answer them, and the figures that go into the Overleaf main text. Everything not listed here is left out of the manuscript. All numbers are computed live from `data/processed/`.
:::

# 1. The variables

The subject of every effect statement is **beaver-engineering**, the physical modification beavers create, because the upstream–downstream contrast measures the reach as a whole.

```{r variable-table}
#| echo: false
kable(tribble(
  ~Symbol, ~Name, ~Definition, ~`Meaning (unit)`, ~`Question it answers`,
  "$\\text{DOC}_{up,s}$, $\\text{DOC}_{down,s}$", "upstream DOC, downstream DOC", "measured",
  "DOC concentration entering / leaving the beaver-engineered reach in season $s$ ($w$ = winter, $s$ = summer) **(mg L$^{-1}$)**",
  "What is the DOC concentration before and after the beaver-engineered reach in each season?",
  "$\\Delta\\text{DOC}_s$", "local response", "$\\text{DOC}_{down,s} - \\text{DOC}_{up,s}$",
  "the change in DOC that beaver-engineering produces in season $s$; positive = enrichment, negative = depletion **(mg L$^{-1}$)**",
  "Does beaver-engineering increase or decrease DOC, and by how much, in each season?",
  "$S$", "inherited seasonal contrast", "$\\text{DOC}_{up,summer} - \\text{DOC}_{up,winter}$",
  "the winter-to-summer change of upstream DOC, i.e. what the upstream river corridor delivers to the reach **(mg L$^{-1}$)**",
  "How much does DOC change between winter and summer in the river before it reaches the beaver-engineered reach?",
  "$R_s$", "relative response", "$\\Delta\\text{DOC}_s / \\lvert S \\rvert$",
  "how much DOC beaver-engineering adds ($R_s > 0$) or removes ($R_s < 0$) in season $s$, as a fraction of the inherited seasonal contrast **(dimensionless)**",
  "How much does beaver-engineering add or remove DOC, relative to the inherited seasonal contrast?",
  "$A_\\text{beaver}$, $A_\\text{floodplain}$", "areas", "mapped",
  "ponded footprint of the beaver-engineered reach; contributing catchment floodplain area **(km$^2$)**",
  "How large is the beaver-engineered footprint, and how large is the floodplain that generates $S$?",
  "$F$", "footprint contrast", "$A_\\text{floodplain} / A_\\text{beaver}$",
  "how much larger the floodplain area is than the beaver-engineered footprint **(dimensionless)**",
  "How small is the beaver-engineered footprint relative to the floodplain that generates $S$?"))
```

![**Derivation of the variables.** Top: the same causal structure operates in winter and summer; downstream DOC inherits upstream DOC and is modified by local hydrological and biological processes. Bottom (dashed): $\Delta\text{DOC}_s$, $S$, $R_s$ and $F$ are calculations from the observed or latent concentrations, not causal nodes. Solid arrows are causal pathways; the green arrow is the persistence of the hydrologic template between seasons.](../images/DAG_variable_derivation.png){#fig-dag}

# 2. Research questions and hypotheses

| \# | Research question | Hypothesis | Answered by | Figure |
|-------------|-----------------|-----------------|-------------|-------------|
| **Q1 Direction** | Does beaver-engineering consistently increase or decrease DOC downstream compared with upstream? | No consistent direction: responses are variable and heavy-tailed, shifted toward enrichment in summer when primary production is highest. | $\Delta\text{DOC}_s$ | Fig. 1a |
| **Q2 Drivers** | Which abiotic and biotic drivers set the direction of the local response? | Dams increase water residence time, which promotes primary producers and thereby DOC; high upstream DOC favours retention. | structural causal model | Fig. 1b |
| **Q3 Magnitude** | How much does beaver-engineering add or remove DOC, relative to the inherited seasonal contrast? | In summer the local response is a substantial fraction of the inherited seasonal contrast; in winter it is negligible. | $R_s$, with $F$ as spatial context | Fig. 2 |

# 3. Q1 — Direction

![**Figure 1a. Direction of the local response.** Posterior predictive distribution of $\Delta\text{DOC}_s$ for a single sampling of a beaver-engineered stream, in winter and summer, from the measurement-error model on the raw upstream and downstream concentrations. Shaded areas: posterior predictive probability of depletion ($\Delta\text{DOC}_s < -0.5$ mg L$^{-1}$, coral), of a negligible response (ROPE $\pm 0.5$ mg L$^{-1}$, grey) and of enrichment ($\Delta\text{DOC}_s > 0.5$ mg L$^{-1}$, blue). Point: median; bars: 66% and 95% intervals.](../overleaf/figures/media/Figure_2a.png){#fig-q1}

```{r q1-data}
m <- read.csv(here("data", "processed", "m12.csv"))
w <- m |> filter(season == "winter") |> select(site, beaver_territory, up_w = DOC_input, dn_w = DOC_out,
                                                 Afp = A_floodplain_km2, Abv = A_beaver_km2)
s <- m |> filter(season == "summer") |> select(site, beaver_territory, up_s = DOC_input, dn_s = DOC_out)
d <- inner_join(w, s, by = c("site", "beaver_territory")) |> filter(complete.cases(up_w, dn_w, up_s, dn_s)) |>
  mutate(dw = dn_w - up_w, ds = dn_s - up_s, F = Afp / Abv)
sw <- d |> summarise(n = n(), winter_enrich = mean(dw > 0), summer_enrich = mean(ds > 0),
                     dep_to_enr = sum(dw < 0 & ds > 0), enr_to_dep = sum(dw > 0 & ds < 0))
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Key message of @fig-q1

Beaver-engineering does **not** change DOC in a consistent direction. The average local response is negligible (+0.14 mg L$^{-1}$ in summer, 0.00 in winter, both inside the ROPE), but a single sampling is broad and heavy-tailed: about 76% negligible, 12–16% enrichment, 9–12% depletion, with a slight prevalence of enrichment in summer.

One sentence to add to the Results: of the `r sw$n` reaches with both seasons, `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100*sw$winter_enrich)` show enrichment in winter and `r sprintf("%.0f%%", 100*sw$summer_enrich)` in summer; `r sw$dep_to_enr` reaches switch from winter depletion to summer enrichment, `r sw$enr_to_dep` the other way.

**Placement: main text, Figure 1a** (unchanged).
:::

# 4. Q2 — Drivers

![**Figure 1b. Drivers of the local response.** Structural causal model with the estimated standardized effects; solid edges carry at least 90% posterior probability of a directional effect, dashed edges are inconclusive.](../images/Capitani_Figure_2b.png){#fig-q2}

::: {.callout-note}
## Key message of @fig-q2

The direction of the local response is set by the context the pond receives: upstream DOC has the largest total effect (−0.10; high upstream DOC favours retention), followed by solar radiation acting through the primary producers (+0.04). The number of dams and the dam height act only weakly, through water residence time. Beaver-engineering creates the conditions; the inputs decide the sign.

**Placement: main text, Figure 1b** (unchanged). Supporting material stays in Appendix S1 (hypotheses table, priors, checks, total effects, alternative connectivity model).
:::

# 5. Q3 — Magnitude: the relative response $R_s$

$R_s$ is computed from the **latent** concentrations of a Bayesian hierarchical measurement-error model (one model per measured concentration, log scale, 0.2 mg L$^{-1}$ instrument error; `notebook/latent_concentrations_fit.R`), so the ratio is never formed from raw values and its uncertainty is carried through. Draws below: `r nrow(readRDS(here("results","latent_R_thin.rds"))$S)` posterior draws per reach.

```{r q3-compute}
LR <- readRDS(here("results", "latent_R_thin.rds"))     # thinned copy of results/latent_R.rds
R_s <- LR$R_s; R_w <- LR$R_w; S_lat <- LR$S
medR  <- function(R, keep = rep(TRUE, ncol(R))) apply(R[, keep, drop = FALSE], 1, median)
absS  <- apply(abs(S_lat), 2, median)
qf    <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", median(x), quantile(x, .025), quantile(x, .975))
q3 <- tibble(
  Quantity = c("Median $R_{summer}$ across reaches", "Median $R_{winter}$ across reaches",
               "$R_{summer} - R_{winter}$",
               "Median $R_{summer}$, excluding the 20% smallest $\\lvert S \\rvert$ (ratio-stability check)"),
  `Posterior median [95% CrI]` = c(qf(medR(R_s)), qf(medR(R_w)), qf(medR(R_s) - medR(R_w)),
                                   qf(medR(R_s, absS > quantile(absS, .2)))),
  `P(> 0)` = sprintf("%.3f", c(mean(medR(R_s) > 0), mean(medR(R_w) > 0), mean(medR(R_s) - medR(R_w) > 0),
                               mean(medR(R_s, absS > quantile(absS, .2)) > 0))))
kable(q3)
n_add <- sum(colMeans(R_s > 0) > 0.9); n_rem <- sum(colMeans(R_s < 0) > 0.9)
```

```{r fig-R}
#| fig-height: 8.5
#| fig-cap: "**Figure 2. Relative response $R_s$ of beaver-engineering, by season.** (a) Posterior distribution of the median relative response across the 158 reaches, in winter and summer; point: posterior median, bars: 66% and 95% credible intervals; the dashed line marks no response. (b) Relative response of each reach in summer: posterior median and 90% credible interval, reaches ranked by their median. Blue: beaver-engineering adds DOC with posterior probability above 0.9; vermillion: removes DOC with probability above 0.9; grey: undetermined. The grey band marks $\\lvert R_{summer} \\rvert < 0.1$. Pseudo-log axis."
pop <- bind_rows(tibble(season = "summer", v = medR(R_s)), tibble(season = "winter", v = medR(R_w))) |>
  mutate(season = factor(season, levels = c("winter", "summer")))
pa <- ggplot(pop, aes(x = v, y = season, fill = season)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey45") +
  stat_halfeye(.width = c(.66, .95), point_interval = "median_qi", alpha = .85, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(summer = OK[["vermillion"]], winter = OK[["green"]])) +
  labs(x = expression("Median relative response across reaches,  "*R[s]*" = "*Delta*DOC[s]*" / |S|"), y = NULL) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

per <- tibble(med = apply(R_s, 2, median), lo = apply(R_s, 2, quantile, .05), hi = apply(R_s, 2, quantile, .95),
              p_add = colMeans(R_s > 0)) |>
  mutate(class = case_when(p_add > 0.9 ~ "adds DOC (P > 0.9)", p_add < 0.1 ~ "removes DOC (P > 0.9)", TRUE ~ "undetermined")) |>
  arrange(med) |> mutate(rank = row_number())
psl <- pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 0.1, base = 10)
pb <- ggplot(per, aes(x = rank, y = med, colour = class)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -0.1, ymax = 0.1, fill = "grey88", alpha = .8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey45") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = .55) + geom_point(size = 1.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("adds DOC (P > 0.9)" = OK[["blue"]], "removes DOC (P > 0.9)" = OK[["vermillion"]],
                                 "undetermined" = "grey55"), name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = psl, breaks = c(-10, -1, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 1, 10)) +
  labs(x = "Reach (ranked by posterior median)", y = expression(R[summer]*" (pseudo-log axis)")) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top")
fig2 <- pa / pb + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.3)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")
ggsave(here("results", "figures", "plan", "fig_R.png"), fig2, width = 9, height = 8.5, dpi = 300)
fig2
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Key message of @fig-R

**In summer, beaver-engineering adds DOC equal to about one fifth of the inherited seasonal contrast; in winter it adds nothing.** The median relative response across reaches is `r sprintf("%.2f", median(medR(R_s)))` in summer (95% CrI `r sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", quantile(medR(R_s), .025), quantile(medR(R_s), .975))`, P(> 0) = `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(medR(R_s) > 0))`) and `r sprintf("%.2f", median(medR(R_w)))` in winter. This average conceals two-sided behaviour: in summer `r n_add` reaches add DOC and `r n_rem` remove it with posterior probability above 0.9. The result holds when the reaches with the smallest inherited seasonal contrast are excluded, so it is not driven by small denominators.

Spatial context, one sentence in the text: the beaver-engineered footprint is at the median `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * median(1 / d$F))` of the floodplain area that generates the inherited seasonal contrast ($F$ = `r sprintf("%.0f", median(d$F))`).

**Placement: main text, Figure 2.** It replaces the amplification-factor figure.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
## What changes in the manuscript

1.  The amplification factor $M$ and its figure are removed; Q3 is answered by $R_s$ with $F$ stated once as context.
2.  The abstract sentence "amplified DOC concentration changes 141 times in summer and 33 times in winter" is replaced by the $R_s$ statement above.
3.  The Methods gain the definitions of $S$ and $R_s$ and the latent-concentration model; the $M$ equations are dropped.
:::
